title: PRESSER | Mike Bianco - Fall Ball Wrap-Up (11-16-26)
text: How did uh fall go? >> Um it was a good fall. You know uh one of the things I've said you know several times u you know when you get to the fall one of the things is you know just to try to get everything in you know systemwise offensively defensively you know pitching wise but certainly you know it's a valuation especially in today's day where you know half of the roster is new every fall is you know to just see guys for the first time on the field. um rather than a computer screen. Um uh but with that as we've known you over the last few years. Um the the fall is just a snapshot and sometimes it's hard to uh to see you know guys some guys don't have a great fall and uh one of the interesting things I think about this fall is um how many guys had good falls. you know, [snorts] how many new guys, you know, had good falls, you know, from pitchers and hitters. Um, you know, some of the guys you just spoke to, you know, Fields and and Foster and others that had really really good falls. Um, so, you know, going into winter break and, you know, not going to be able to see them for for a little bit, you know, that makes you feel a lot better. >> Is it is it pretty easy to uh you've been through it so much when a pitcher comes in and you shut him down for the fall. Is that an easy decision or a hard decision or how does that work? I you know it not so much for the for the uh the returners and I think uh and that happens more with those guys and there's been some guys even you know last year where um and some something like Charlie you know uh where um you want to do what's right obviously for for for the kids and for health reasons but you know for somebody like Hooks who you've seen and you've seen him at his very best returning all-American a guy that pitched for the USA national team. Um I I think it's takes, you know, u no um when the pitching coach comes to you and says, "I think this is the best way, you know, to to handle him this fall is maybe shut him down here at the very beginning, let him get back in the weight room and then ramp him back up." I think that's an easy decision. Uh it's a little harder with the new guys just because you want to see them, you know, and and get get a chance to see them. So, um, but you know, again, a lot goes into that, Joel. You know, depending on who they are, what they are, and a lot of times, like those two guys, it has nothing to do with injuries. It has more to do with how much they threw, when they threw, and where they are when they get here. >> I came to a lot of the inner squad games. It seems like you got a real competitive >> environment out there. Is that how you see it as well? Yeah, just about every position. >> Yeah. and and you know, you hope that's part of your culture. You know, part of how we play the inner squad games and there's something on the line and um you know, our our inner squad games on the weekend are process based. So, they're more than just the runs. It's you know, as you know by now, they're they're they're judged by quality at bats, quality pitches, certain things that we're emphasizing in each inter squad game. So, there's a lot more on the line. Part of that is one, you're teaching them the game. You're teaching them the process, but the other part is it gives them a way to win the game, to have success besides the actual runs that are being scored. And so I think it just keeps everybody more involved. And so, and I think the other part of that is you got a lot of new faces, you know, and and those those guys, this is the first time they've been out. We talked about this first time we got to see him, but you know, this is the first time, you know, they that they're on our stage and and so um certainly there's there's there's an energy level to that as well. >> Since we just talked to Charlie Foster, tell us a little bit more about him from your perspective and how he's done. Well, terrific, you know, and uh not arguably. I mean, I I would think it would be hard to argue if anybody pitched better than he did this fall and we had a lot of guys that pitched well. Uh but you made some adjustments, you know, over the summer and certainly since he's been here with Joel, uh mechanically and and everything has just ticked up for him, you know, and uh velocity uh command u all his pitches. I mean, he's he's he's had as about as dominant fall as you can have. >> A lefty at 99, >> it's pretty strong, is it? >> It is. Uh, but it but it's more than that. And that's, you know, uh, and we know now, you know, velocity matters, but it's only part of the equation. Um, and certainly it's the one that everybody sees and it's on the scoreboard and all of that, but we've we've watched and we've had guys in the program like everybody else has that there's some big numbers up their velocity, but that's not the only, you know, only factor and and sometimes that gets hit. Um and you know to to his credit not only has he like I said not only has the velocity increased but the command has increased the uh the different you know breaking ball ball arsenals have has uh I think helped him and u you know so not only did he only I think walk maybe two guys the entire fall but he struck out 20 plus guys. It's just yeah it's been pretty dominant for him. >> You got a lot of lefties this year. I'm sure that was by design. >> It was, you know, uh, but again, you just don't want left-handed pitchers. You want left-handed pitchers that can help you. And so, uh, when you look through at guys like Pillsbury, you certainly, you know, you return to Hooks and Elliott, then you add Foster and and Pillsbury and, uh, Carrie and and, uh, I'm sure I'm going to be missing somebody else in there. Um, you know, uh, obviously those guys are going to, you know, bring a lot of depth, some different roles. One of the things that we we you know uh haven't talked a lot about because so many guys were brought in. We we lose two first rounders that pitched on the weekend for us and or started on the weekend. And so we got to uh fill some holes there and and and some some big bullpin pieces as well. And so where would that all play out? You know, we're still probably, you know, um you know, trying to discover and figure figure it out, not just now, but you know, as we get into to the early spring and probably leading into the first few weeks of the season. Uh but the good news is there's there's a lot of guys and not just left-handed guys, but a lot of guys that I can think give us length. So it means they can start, they can be, you know, good bullpin pieces and not just guys that u are left-handed matchup type of guys. A lot of talk about pitching in this conversation. What about your offense hitters? What would you >> Yeah, I thought it was good. Um, you know, another guy that you just talked to, Blake Fields, I thought had a terrific fall and like the pitchers. A lot of those new guys played well. You know, Ksky had a really good fall. Hoy, uh, transfer from Louisiana Tech led the the, um, you know, the team in hitting, you know, throughout the fall. So, a lot of the new faces played well. Winston Pennet, true freshman. uh you know played really well in the outfield. Uh Christian Dodie played really well probably the second half of the fall. Uh so some of those new Brady Dallore almost forgot you started to think infielder outfielderfielder. How about the catchers? Uh Brady Dalamore you know another new face that uh I thought you know swung it well played really well behind the plate and not to mention the returners. You just talked to Decker, uh, Pino, um, you know, I thought Pereira, you know, who's the one of, you know, the returning catcher that, you know, played really well on both sides of the ball. Uh, Fed, you know, had a terrific fall as he, you know, usually has. So, you know, a lot of guys that swung it well. >> Yeah, we don't forget catchers in this program. >> There you go. Catchers are important. Is is this a situation where you might be able to uh platoon more and play more guys particularly midweek? Somebody asked me that the other day and u you know we try to do that but at the end of the day once you get to conference play by mid-March you're hopeful that you know not that that lineup gets written in stone but you know when you go out there to play Florida or Mississippi State or LSU or some you know some opponent in the Southeastern Conference that you're putting your best nine out there right uh and and so to me it's important to kind of figure that out. So it's hard to do that just in the fall. uh things can change. You know, this is like I said at the very beginning, this is just a snapshot of, you know, what what what you know what the I think the season has in store. And so, we'll see as we get to February 19th, they'll there'll certainly be some platooning. Um, one of the things that you want to set them up for success, you know, especially the new guys. So, sometimes that happens where it's a righty left hander matchup and it's really done not because this guy can't play against a righthander or a left-hander. really to set up the guy that's in to have success. And so eventually, uh, you try to figure that out. Sometimes it's not. Sometimes you get to to the middle of March and you you still are moving some guys in versus, you know, right-handed pitcher and left-handed pitching. And so, uh, that was a complicated answer to it. Could be. >> Yeah. >> Yeah. Is there an update on you tomorrow and Furnace at all? >> No, not yet. Um, if Furnace is eligible, you got quite a battle at first with Aussie, you know, is he is he DH material? >> We're we're already uh t talking about the uh the the quarterback controversy. [laughter] Um, well, here and here's one of the things. Um, and it happens every fall and I get it and it's the excitement of baseball and program and this is fall baseball like there's spring football and you know at the end of the day I don't think we've ever gotten to May and say we have too many good hitters. I don't think we've ever gotten to May and you know 26 years and say hey we got too much pitching. We just we just don't know who to what good guy to put in there right now. And so at the end of the day it will all play out uh and everybody will find their spot. How successful is the team at using the ABS this fall? >> Um, that's it's been interesting. You know, we've had some good days and bad days. Pizza Bowl was probably the worst day where maybe some of you guys have seen it. Um, and that's one of the things I think like everything else, we kind of got to work on a little bit. We can't just say it'll take care of itself because it's new and it's new to everybody. We'll have to come up with a, you know, a little bit of a a philosophy or system of how we approach it. Uh, but you know, I think it's a good thing. You know, we uh I think we've said for years in college baseball that we'd like our rules to to to mirror Major League Baseball and and you know, because of finances, because of technology and everything else. And um usually we're a few years behind them, but it eventually gets our way like you know uh instant replay and other things. And so, uh, this is just another one of those, you know, pieces that I think, uh, you know, is our game trying to mirror the major league game. And like I think you, if you ask most major league organizations, they've evolved, right? And how they use it, how good they become of it. U, probably like anything else, there'll be some guys that are better at it than others. Uh, and we'll have to evaluate that, too. But, uh, it's it's been I don't want to just say fun because it's not for us, it's it's part of the game, right? It's part of the rules. Uh and we want to be able to utilize it in the best manner that gives us the best u I think uh road to success. Uh that's important. I know it'll be exciting for the fans and people see it and the win loss people ch you know clapping for a ball strike you know 45 seconds after the pitch. Um but but also the reason you do it is those things matter. you know, a ball or strike called in the third inning or sixth inning. You know, sometimes, you know, sways a count one way or the other, which sometimes changes the game. And so, in our in our day, our game, it's it's super important. >> What is the rule? You get three a game. >> Three, you get three misses a game, right? >> Three misses. Okay. If you get it right, it doesn't count. >> Three. Exactly. You know, uh Golden. Yeah. Golden we we uh he's had one of those statistically if you look at his fall it wasn't what wasn't the greatest but man did he play really well you know and so performed really well. uh had some bad fortune, you know, as far far as calls with, you know, some of the player umpires out there. Um, and just one of those things where a lot of quality at bats and proud of the way he's played, he had a really good summer. You know, Bull after the injury last year, bounced back, had had a had a really good fall. You know, Toeer as well. So, some of those new faces, you know, Pino I thought was excellent. I don't know if he made an error the entire fall was terrific. Um, I I mentioned Pereira, you know, has played played really well. So, um, yeah, I I it was a it was a good fall, you know, uh, for for for a lot of the guys and and that's again unusual, you know, so many new guys got off to good starts. Um, you know, I think, uh, you know, offensively and on the mound, it was kind of split where usually it's a fall where it's either dominated by the pitching or it's dominated by the hitters. And I think it's we've had a little bit of both. >> Thank you, brother. >> All right, we good. Look.
